recipes.name: Camp David Spaghetti with Italian Sausage

steps.text: Slice sausages lengthwise, leaving links attached along one side; lay flat in a large skillet. Cook over medium heat until browned and cooked through, 5 minutes, flipping once. Transfer to a plate; set aside.

Add ground beef, onion, garlic, and olive oil to the same skillet over medium heat; cook and stir until onion is translucent and beef is browned and crumbly, about 10 minutes. Drain all but 2 tablespoons drippings from the skillet.

Stir in tomato sauce, tomatoes, oregano, salt, basil, bay leaf, and black pepper; simmer, uncovered, over low heat until flavors have blended, about 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Remove and discard bay leaf.

Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook spaghetti in the boiling water, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain.
Divide spaghetti and sauce among individual oven-safe baking dishes or plates; top each with a cooked half sausage and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until cheese is melted and begins to brown, 5 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Camp David Spaghetti with Italian Sausage
raw_recipe.description: This Camp David spaghetti with Italian sausage features hearty ground beef, tomato pasta sauce, spaghetti, Italian sausage, and Parmesan cheese.

review.reviewBody: when i looked over this recipe, i couldnt figure out why nobody had reviewed it because it sounded so good. so i decided to give it a try. i made it for my boyfriend and my family for valentines day. my family loves spaghetti and they thought this recipe was fantastic! it is one of the best sauces i have ever tried and made. i highly suggest it!!! i made afew minor changes but mainly stuck to the recipe. it is so flavorful! if you are looking for a good sauce i would try this one. changes i made: cut the sausage into tiny meatballs instead of lenghtwise added all of the juice from the whole tomotoes added extra basil and oragano to taste

Indeed the best spaghetti I've made at home thus far (my husband's favorite spaghetti). Gave it four stars because the amount of salt was a bit too much for us, so I reduced it to less than 1/4 tsp... we could probably do without added salt altogether. We've made it with and without sausage- both good. Also made it with 1 Tbsp. dried oregano vs. fresh... great that way too. Thank you for the recipe!

The bones of this sauce are good, but I felt it needed something... I used 3 links of sausage instead of 2. Like other reviewers, I sliced in half and cooked, and then crumbled it in while simmering. I also added an entire 28 oz can (juice and all) of whole peeled tomatoes, but cut them into smaller pieces as I have picky family members. I couldn't find fresh oregano at the store, so used dry in 1/2 the amount. After all together, my taster told me the sauce needed more depth to counter the salt and meat, so I added 1 can of tomato paste, 1 c of water, and about 1 T of sugar. Now it's perfect!

Well..well..well...what can I say that hasn't already been said?? This is THE BEST spaghetti I have ever tasted or made in my entire life!! It got rave reviews from my family and neighbor. Followed the recipe to a T..I always saute my fresh mushrooms and onions in olive oil and butter before adding to a recipe, I just love the flavor of the mushrooms....anyway probably added a little more garlic that called for but other than that right to the recipe. We really liked the fact that it wasn't so "tomatoey", yum, it was absolutely delicious!! This will be my go to recipe from now on..the search is over! I would love to know if this "navy chef" has any more recipes...I served this with Giada D. cheddar onion bread..my god it is wonderful, also. Thanks so much for sharing this recipe...I truly appreciate it.

I made a few small changes due to what I had on hand. I increased the garlic, I did not add the full amount of salt (just enough for flavor) and I drained off the liquid in the tomatoes and replaced the liquid I drained off with red wine. I did not have fresh oregano so I used dried. Very nice basic spaghetti sauce that was quick to prepare. I don't think it had too much meat, I think it was just right. Out of the whole skilletful, there is a small bowl of leftovers--I'd say my family liked it!

Made this a 2nd time with another slight modification - it is now my new favorite sauce recipe! Doubled the recipe to have some for freezing...used 1 lb ground hot italian sausage (the spice was what was missing the first time), 2 lbs lean ground beef. Left out the olive oil and browned the meat w/ onions & garlic. Still didn't have fresh oregano, this time I only used 7tsp dried oregano instead of the 8 tsp it should've been...simmered for a bit over an hour. Perfect!

Added 14 cup dried parsley, 1 can 8 0z. mushrooms, (fresh, sauted in butter first would be better)

I cut the sausage into bite sized pieced before adding to sauce. Layered the pasta, sauce, cheese. Baked as directed.
The hour cooking, uncovered is a must do.
I did not have spaghetti pasta. Substituted wide egg noodles. Could not wait for another trip to the grocery. Will use spaghetti next time.
Did not have oven proof plates. Used one 9 x 13 LeCruset casserole. Grandson Said, "Oh, a casserole." He ate like any 18 year old growing 6'2" boy. Will make again.

There are only two in our family so, I only used one sausage, and eight ounces of ground turkey, but went according to recipe for the amounts of tomato sauce and canned tomatoes. The sauce did cook down considerably, and there was definitely enough meat. Other than cooking the two meats together, I made it according to recipe. The flavor was really good, so I will be making it again. It really did surprise me how tasty it was with so few ingredients, but it was a very pleasant surprise. It is on my "tried it, loved it!" list.

Really enjoyed making this, easy directions to follow. And I followed them for a change. Used fresh oregano and dried basil, but probably could use Italian seasoning if you didn’t have the fresh herb. Oregano is like a weed in my herb barrel, so it was super mild tasting. I used a large deep Pyrex dish rather than individual ones. Baked for 10 minutes to melt the cheese. I’ll make this again for a crowd!

I thought this was pretty good. There just seemed to be something missing. I got a little worried when I tasted it at first, but as it cooked the taste began to come out more. I put this in a crockpot along with the sausage and let it simmer/cook on low for 5 hours.

My whole family loves this spaghetti sauce. Fresh oregano is critical to the fantastic taste, it's worth the effort, trust me. My tiny changes include using a pound of hot Italian sausage, crumbled and cooked with the ground beef, and adding about a 1/2 cup of pasta water to the sauce when the pasta is finished cooking. I serve the pasta and sauce separately, my preference.
Over the moon delicious.

This was a wonderful recipe. I made it as the recipe suggested except I used diced tomatoes instead of whole peeled tomatoes. I also used angel hair instead of Spaghetti. Finally, I used 1lb ground hot Italian sausage and cut it into 4 squares and divided the spaghetti into 4 individual oven safe bowls. This is definitely something I will make over and over.
Great taste, but it seemed there was too much pasta compared to the meat sauce.
Like 👍
it looks easy to make and maybe my family will eat with all ingredients in the dish
My first mstake was picking up the spaghitti and threw it into the pot, then as I laid the box down find I had cooked angel hair!Yikes!! IT will be alright. Supper is going to be a treat. Can't wait!

This was tasty thanks in large part to the flavorful Italian sausages, but I thought the dish was too meaty and not saucy enough. I made only minor changes, including: used impossible meat instead of real beef, doubled the garlic, and used two bay leaves. Additional changes I would make in the future: decrease or eliminate the beef, increase the whole tomatoes to a 28 oz can, remove casings from the sausage and crumble on top of dish before baking, add some red pepper flakes, and increase the Parmesan cheese to 3/4 cup. Maybe increase the baking time a bit as well as I didn't notice much of a difference. Creates ample leftovers for two people, which is nice!
Oregano overpowers the dish. Use 1/2 suggested
This is our favorite spaghetti sauce recipe. I've made sauce for years from scratch, by memory. It was pretty good, but this is excellent! And so easy to make.
Made it about 3 months ago and I have made it 4 times since then! The whole family really loves this recipe thanks HungryGuy.
